This method didn't require metal or any external fuel. The name "Baghdad Battery" is derived from the belief that this device was used for treating skin diseases, particularly leprosy. It involved applying the sulfur and tar mixture directly to affected areas. The treatment process relied on electrolysis to produce electricity, which could be used in various medical applications. In summary, the Baghdad Battery is not just a historical curiosity but a testament to the ingenuity of ancient civilizations in discovering electricity using simple yet effective processes.
